footerNote: H125 / AS350 B3 (2B1) training reference. For training use only. Always cross-check with the latest approved RFM.

procedures.title: BEFORE START / PREFLIGHT AND PRE-START CHECKS

right: On board and current. Verify all required documents and check that applicable revisions are incorporated.
Confirm that all corrective maintenance necessary for flightworthiness is completed (Section 4.2).
Perform preflight inspection per RFM Section 4.2, including MGB and TGB oil levels, rotor blades, controls, cowls and leaks. If parked > 2 days or in case of doubt, open cowls.
Check weight, CG and loading are within Section 2 limitations; record any exceedance as required by Section 4.1.
Before the first flight of the day and if OAT is at or above 0 °C, bleed the fuel tank at the drain point and confirm no leakage at the bleed valve.
Secure baggage and cabin freight in accordance with cabin loading instructions and placards.
Check ELT in
position and configure radios, transponder and navigation equipment as required.
Select [BAT/EPU] or external power as applicable. Verify DC voltages within limits.
Rotor brake released, lever fully forward before engine start (Section 4.3).
Forward, with guard in place. Confirm fuel system configured for start, fuel quantity sufficient and approved fuel per Section 2.5.
IDLE position for prestart checks.
UP position. Verify engine control and VEMD powered.
OFF, then select START according to RFM procedure, monitoring Ng, t4 and oil pressure.
Monitor t4 and Ng during start; abort in case of abnormal rise or failure to accelerate as per limitations and emergency procedures.
Allow engine to stabilize in ground idle. Check VEMD indications and absence of abnormal warnings.
Complete remaining checks and progress to rotor engagement according to Section 4.3.
At ground idle and then flight condition, verify Ng, Nf/NR, Tq and t4 within normal operating ranges.
Check full and free movement in all axes, friction adjusted as required, no abnormal forces or stops.
No red warnings; only expected advisories on CWP and VEMD before lift-off.
Establish a stable hover in HIGE at around 5 ft (1.5 m). Check attitude, power required and control response.

In HIGE at about 5 ft (1.5 m) before initiating forward flight, raise collective slightly to confirm that Ng can increase by at least 1 % without exceeding the maximum transient rating, and that the torque required is compatible with the take-off/landing environment and weight (Section 5.1).
Complete remaining checklist items (instruments, doors, harnesses, lights) prior to forward flight.
From a stabilized hover or low-speed run, smoothly accelerate while maintaining NR within limits.

Accelerate towards Vy for best rate of climb. As a guide, Vy is approximately 65 kt IAS at sea level and decreases by about 1 kt for each 1000 ft of pressure altitude (≈ 120 km/h minus 2 km/h per 300 m).

At high internal gross weight, use HIGE power to accelerate along the take-off path until IAS reaches about 40 kt, then begin the climb so as to clear roughly 20 ft (6 m) at around 50 kt (93 km/h), in line with the height–velocity diagram guidance (SUP.28).
Maintain power within MCP or applicable take-off limits; monitor Tq and t4 margins.
Establish climb at Vy or as required by obstacle and terrain; monitor Hp and temperature limits.
Complete after take-off checklist when safely established in climb.

procedures.title: CLIMB
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM Section 4.5 §1 and Section 5.1

right: Above about 100 ft (30 m) AGL, establish a stable climb attitude with NR in the normal range and power within the recommended continuous or take-off ratings.

For maximum climb performance, use Vy. As a guide, Vy ≈ 65 kt IAS at sea level, reducing by about 1 kt per 1000 ft of pressure altitude (≈ 120 km/h minus 2 km/h per 300 m). Adjust as required for obstacles and ATC.
Monitor Tq and t4, keeping margins to transient and maximum limits. Adjust collective to keep a steady climb rate and avoid over-torque or over-temperature.
Approaching cruise altitude, smoothly reduce collective while adjusting cyclic to accelerate or decelerate to desired cruise speed, avoiding abrupt attitude changes.
Complete any after-climb checklist items when stabilized in cruise (pressurization, engine instruments, fuel).

procedures.title: CRUISE FLIGHT AND MANEUVERS
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM Section 4.5 §2 and Section 5.1

right: Establish cruise at a speed and torque setting compatible with fuel planning and limitations; use Section 5.1 tables as a reference.
Over noise-sensitive areas, the complementary manual recommends IAS ≈ 110 kt (204 km/h) for OAT +25 °C, adjusted slightly with temperature, and at least 1000 ft AGL where possible.
Trim the helicopter for hands-light flight where possible to reduce pilot workload and improve stability.
Perform turns and basic maneuvers with smooth, coordinated control inputs, respecting bank angle, load factor and speed limitations given in Sections 2 and 4.5.
Continuously monitor engine/vehicle instruments, fuel balance, and navigation; adjust power and attitude to maintain stable flight.
Plan top-of-descent and brief the approach, taking into account terrain, airspace and weather.

procedures.title: DESCENT AND APPROACH
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM Section 4.5 §3 and Section 5.1

right: Reduce collective smoothly to start descent, keeping NR within normal range and avoiding abrupt power changes.

Adjust cyclic and collective to achieve a stabilized descent profile. For noise-sensitive helipads, use about 60 kt (111 km/h) with a rate of descent close to 1000 ft/min; for approaches near sensitive areas but landing elsewhere, use Vy with around 500 ft/min as a reference.
Monitor Tq, t4, Ng and NR; avoid prolonged low-power descents outside of the conditions allowed by the RFM, and respect all limitations.

Transition from en-route descent to the final approach by aligning with the landing site, confirming wind and obstacles and configuring lights and avionics as required. Plan to be around 100 ft (30 m) AGL when reducing towards a HIGE hover at roughly 5 ft (1.5 m).
Complete approach/landing checks before entering low-level or confined-area segments of the approach.
Assess landing site, slope and wind; ensure slope and surface are within limitations (Section 2.3).

Plan a stabilized approach, managing airspeed and rate of descent within normal envelopes. As a guide, begin the approach around Vy (see climb section) and, in noise-sensitive areas, consider 60 kt (111 km/h) with a rate of descent close to 1000 ft/min or Vy with about 500 ft/min when approaching a helipad near sensitive areas.
Transition to hover as needed; maintain safe clearance and cross-check instruments and power.

Lower collective smoothly to touch down, maintaining attitude and heading with cyclic and pedals. For any planned running landing in normal operations, keep ground speed well below the 40 kt (74 km/h) running landing limitation (Section 2.3).
Stabilize helicopter on ground, then complete post-landing checks and prepare for shutdown as applicable.

procedures.title: ENGINE SHUTDOWN AND SECURING THE HELICOPTER

right: At ground idle, verify engine and vehicle parameters within limits and note any abnormal indications.
Apply normal shutdown procedure from the RFM, including twist grip to IDLE then OFF as prescribed.

Allow rotor to decelerate per limitations. If rotor brake is used, apply it below approximately 170 rpm in high wind conditions or below 140 rpm in normal conditions, as specified in Section 4.6. In high-wind operations, starting and stopping the rotor has been demonstrated up to about 40 kt (74 km/h) from any direction and 50 kt (93 km/h) headwind; for winds above roughly 40 kt, park the helicopter into wind and tie it down per Section 4.8.
Switch off unnecessary consumers, then [GEN], [BAT/EPU] or external power according to shutdown sequence.
Install control locks or collective friction as required, fit covers and blade tie-downs per Section 4.2 guidance.
Stabilized level flight at a power rating close to MCP with Hp ≤ 12000 ft and heating/demisting OFF.
Select the ENGINE POWER CHECK page on the VEMD and perform the check according to Section 5.1.
Check that TRQ MARGIN is positive and T4 MARGIN is negative with
displayed; engine health check is satisfactory in this case.
If VEMD result is not clearly satisfactory, record Tq, Ng, NR, Hp, OAT and t4 and apply the manual ENGINE POWER CHECK and t4 CHECK charts per RFM.

When necessary, compute corrected t4 margin using the Hp/OAT correction table. This correction only applies when the initial T4 margin is ≥ +35 °C; if the corrected margin is negative the result is acceptable, whereas a T4 margin greater than +35 °C means the engine condition is unsatisfactory.

If both VEMD screens fail, the maximum authorized power is the power required to maintain level flight while following the law IAS = 100 kt at 0 Hp minus 2 kt per 1000 ft (or 185 km/h minus 4 km/h per 300 m), as described in Section 3.5.
If margins are unsatisfactory, treat as an engine performance issue and follow maintenance/operational guidance.

procedures.title: CRANKING PROCEDURE
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM – Normal revision 6 / related procedure

right: Use cranking only for the purposes and under the conditions specified in the RFM (e.g. maintenance, engine drying).
Set fuel system, twist grip and engine controls to the positions specified for cranking (no fuel to combustion).
Engage starter according to the RFM, monitoring Ng and respecting starter duty cycle limitations.
Monitor t4, oil pressure and electrical parameters; abort if any abnormal indication occurs.
Allow starter to cool according to limitations before any subsequent start or cranking cycle.
Avoid inhalation of extinguisher agent as much as possible (RFM Section 3.4).
Ventilate the cabin thoroughly to clear smoke and extinguishing agent before continuing operations.
Check affected systems and wiring as required; coordinate with maintenance before next flight.

procedures.title: TAIL ROTOR FAILURE – HANDLING AND LANDING

right: Recognize uncontrolled yaw (typically to the left) and differentiate between loss of thrust and loss of control.
LAND IMMEDIATELY. Reduce twist grip to IDLE and increase collective as required to cushion touch-down as per Section 3.3 §1.1.
Simultaneously reduce collective depending on available height, move cyclic forward to gain speed and maintain Vy or higher, adjusting collective to minimize sideslip (Section 3.3 §1.2).
Maintain Vy or higher and adjust collective to obtain minimum sideslip; LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE on a site suitable for autorotation (Section 3.3 §1.3).

On a suitable area, perform an autorotative landing according to the ENGINE FLAME-OUT autorotation procedure (Section 3.2): maintain about Vy in the descent, flare at roughly 70 ft (21 m), level at around 20-25 ft (6-8 m) and cushion the touchdown with collective. Over water, aim to ditch with IAS below 30 kt (56 km/h) and minimum rate of descent, and keep the twist grip at IDLE during the descent.

In case of pedal jamming/loss of control, avoid airspeeds below about 20 kt, especially near the ground. Set IAS around 70 kt (130 km/h) in level flight, use HYD TEST / ACCU TST as described in Section 3.3 §2 and carry out a shallow running landing with slight left sideslip.
